barCharacter: Vera Oberlin, the same comparison as round 1. She sits at the top of the hierarchy and judges everyone, and her comedy is the status she takes for granted ('cover up the literal murder I've committed... Right?', 'Right. Now.'). That is Vesper's job as a star with standards. Valerie the shopkeeper, with her bored deadpan, is the closest on register, but she has fewer lines and does not judge suitors. The corpus has 9 Vera lines, so the bar's 12 are those 9 plus the 3 narrator lines written about her (#53, #54, #55).

bar: Sorry, I'm focusing on my career... my career on not dating losers like you!

Narrator: You turn around to find Vera staring at you. This often happens, but for some reason it's not a death stare this time.
Narrator: You see Vera at the mirror, attempting to tame her hair with a cattle prod.
Narrator: Whoa. You know this is a serious situation if it's causing Vera to show empathy.
headToHead.voiceVerdict: Bar, but the gap is smaller than in round 1. The rewrite worked: the turn now lands on Vesper (her years, her booth, the trucker, the mast) and not on the suitor's jargon, so with the names covered our top 12 are recognisably hers. They are recognisable by their nouns and premise, though (my show, sixty-two, station owner, my hours, frequency), not by their shape. Nine of the twelve use the same clipped 'Statement. Statement. Kicker.' triplet that Maximilian uses ('Our future. Three words. Exactly three. I'm counting, and I'm petty.') and Pixel uses too. Swap the radio nouns for hotel nouns and the rhythm survives untouched. The persona promises 'languid, low, unhurried', and the page delivers brisk fragments. Vera is unmistakable because the shape is the status move: the repeated-word fake-out ('my career... my career on not dating losers'), the tag 'Right?', the two-word order 'Right. Now.' Cover her nouns and you still know it is her.
headToHead.constructionVerdict: Ours, on the top 12 only. Every one of our twelve lands on its last one to three words. Several turn twice ('He's dead. Still better.', 'I muted the moon landing. I can mute you.'), and none explains itself. Vera's twelve include flat plot hooks (#46, #49, #50) and a 30-word feminism line that only works in context. Across the whole bank this would be a tie at best: the middle relies on tag endings ('Go on.', 'Goodnight.', 'Lovely.', a year) where a turn should be.
headToHead.quotableVerdict: Bar, narrowly. 'I muted the moon landing', 'Moon and June retired on my show in sixty-two', 'I'm changing my hours' and the porch light would get clipped, which is real progress from round 1's two clip-worthy lines. But Vesper's status claims are wistful, and Vera's are outrageous: she assumes you will cover up a murder and she drinks the tears of her enemies. A clip spreads because of the size of the assumption, and Vesper's biggest assumption (she outranks the moon landing) is the only one at Vera's size.

templates: Card label as the opener: '[the card restated]. [remark].' About 22 of the 48 cardReact lines open by naming the card they react to ('Money.', 'Brutal.', 'Verse.', 'Numbers.', 'Decimals.', 'Flattery.', 'Feelings.', 'Pet names.', 'Illegal.', 'A scene.', 'Short.', 'No answer.', 'An apology.', 'Midnight snacks.', 'To the letter.', 'Too true.', 'Lovely word.'). It reads like the writers' room filing a line under its card, and it sets the clipped rhythm for the whole bank.

Year stamp: '[I did your thing first]. [year].' Seventeen lines carry a year or a span of decades ('I was like that in sixty-four.', 'Nineteen sixty-six. Lovely.', 'On air. Seventy-two.', 'Heard that pitch in seventy-four.', 'Like my jingle in sixty-eight.', 'I did that for forty years.', 'Sixty years I've...', 'since seventy-three', 'from sixty-two'). This is the persona's status move, but repeated this often it has become a sign-off, not a joke.

'Nobody has X since [obsolete thing]': 'since disco', 'since the wireless had valves', 'since the switchboard had operators', 'since the engineer retired', 'since the fire', 'since the transistor', 'since before you had a power cord', 'since sixty-one', 'since seventy-three'. Nine lines.

'That's my job / my bit / my slot, I'll want it back': 'That's my deadpan, Crumb. I'll want it back.', 'You finished my sentence. I'm going to need it back.', 'Soothing's my slot.', 'Usually that's my job.', 'stop doing my job badly', 'That's my bit, caller.', 'That's my job, and I'm better at it.', 'Knowing everything. I did that for forty years.' Eight lines, all the same claim of territory.

'I've had better / longer / faster': 'I've had faster callers', 'I've read the tide tables with more feeling', 'judged by better appliances', 'silence that was more romantic', 'I've cried on air once. It was better than that.', 'My hiccups ran longer', 'better offers from the station owner', 'I'm better at it', 'Mine aged better.' Nine lines.

Loneliness as 'Nobody': 19 lines contain 'nobody' ('Nobody called.', 'Nobody does.', 'Nobody's ever watched me.', 'Nobody came.', 'Nobody tuned in.', 'nobody turned it', 'Nobody's dared.', 'Nobody has the nerve.', 'Nobody ever wrote back to mine.', 'Nobody's listening. Nobody usually is.'). The persona asks for the slip four words at a time, now and then. At one line in ten it is no longer a slip but the subject of the show.

Tag endings that stand in for a turn: 'Go on.' (6), 'Goodnight.' (5 of 16 cuts), 'Mm.' (5 openers plus 1 closer), 'Lovely.' (4), 'I'm keeping you' / 'Stay' / 'Stay on' (8 across picks and reacts), the trucker (5).
ruleBreaks: Word limits: none broken. Every category was checked against types.ts (intro 14, questions 18, react 10, cardReact counted at 10, cut 14, twistIntro 18, oneOnOne 14, hold 12, pick 16, outro 12). No em dashes, emoji, exclamation marks, lists, 'as an AI', stock romance filler, real songs, singers, stations or brands. Nothing goes past PG-13.
Borrowed real-world joke: 'Brock, my needles only go to ten. You came in at forty.' This is a famous film's 'goes to eleven' joke with the number changed. No name is used, but it is not hers.
Contradicts the persona (she never sleeps, and 'Go to sleep. I won't.' is one of her best lines): 'I wake up mean. Not cute mean. What do you do, caller?'

Too nice for a cringing react, since it is self-pity that lets Vex off: 'On air my whole life. Nobody's ever watched me.'
Too nice for a cut, an 'it's not you, it's me' letdown: 'Nav, you'd take me somewhere. I don't leave the building. Goodnight.'

biggestGap: Vesper's voice is now carried by her nouns (caller, fader, sixty-two, the trucker) and not by the shape of her sentences: nearly every line is the house's clipped 'Noun. Remark. Kicker.' triplet, the same rhythm Maximilian and Pixel use, while her persona promises languid and unhurried. In the next pass, give her one shape that only she has: a single slow, run-on sentence held together by commas and 'and', with the status claim tossed off in the middle as an aside and the cut as the last quiet word ('I muted the moon landing, caller, and I can mute you' is the model). Strip the card-label openers, year stamps and 'Go on.' / 'Goodnight.' tags that currently do the work a turn should do.

notes: Bar file present and read in full (88 entries plus narration, with its section on what makes the voices unmistakable). charm-notes.md was skimmed. Round 1's verdict was read for continuity. The bank holds 191 lines (an exact match with round 1), and every line was read. The generic share fell from 58.6% to 40.8%. The rewrite fixed round 1's main problem: the suitor's gimmick is now mostly setup and the turn lands on Vesper. The 'strip the gimmick, ask the secret' one-on-ones are gone, so are the 'Say it again, slower' approvals and most of the 'Caller, [rebuke]' lines (3 lines now open on 'Caller', down from 19). Remaining weak spots by category: cardReact is the worst (about 30 of its 48 lines are generic, templated or card-label filler). twistIntro and questions are slots shared with the other stars, and five of them have near twins in maximilian.json or pixel.json; the bank cannot be told apart in those slots except for the Moon and June line, the cut-people-for-four line and 'Mostly mine.' Every Crumb line in oneOnOne and pick has a near twin in Maximilian's bank, because both writers drew on Crumb's 'how done you are' flirt. The dedication device should be her signature, but it splits in two. The formal ones work ('A ballad. Eleven minutes. No clapping.', 'A song with no chorus. It just stops. Like this.', 'Two versions. Both called Goodbye.'). The 'It's called [plain insult]' ones explain the joke. Keep the first kind and cut the second. Also worth protecting: 'I had a fortune once. It's the tall mast outside.', 'Prince, I've had better offers from the station owner. He's dead. Still better.', 'Last grand gesture I got was a skywriter. Misspelled Vesper.', 'Sorry, Tilly. See? It's easy. Goodnight.', 'Our future in three words. Not four. I've cut people for four.', 'That wasn't an answer. That was weather.', 'Illegal. I broadcast pirate from a fishing boat once. Continue.' (a fish on a fishing boat, played straight), and the modem's 'Then her mother picked up the other phone.' To reach Vera's quotability, scale the status claims up to the moon-landing level (an assumption that is outrageous, not just nostalgic) and cut the small ones (jingle sold soap, sixty-four, farm prices).
